label: Ba-La-Cu-O: tentative 30 K onset (1986)
summary: Bednorz and Mueller reported an abrupt resistivity decrease of up to three orders of magnitude in multiphase, oxygen-deficient polycrystalline Ba-La-Cu-O samples, with the highest onset in the 30 K range and suppression at high current density; they described this as reminiscent of percolative superconductivity.

label: Mixed-phase Y-Ba-Cu-O: 80–93 K transition (1987)
summary: NASA’s catalogue summary of Wu et al. reports a stable, reproducible superconductivity transition between 80 and 93 K in a mixed-phase Y-Ba-Cu-O compound system at ambient pressure, maintained in a liquid-nitrogen Dewar.

label: YBCO grain-boundary orientation limits (1988)
summary: Dimos et al. measured grain-boundary critical current densities as a function of basal-plane misorientation in YBCO bicrystals and concluded that strong texture both normal to and within the basal plane is important for very high critical currents in pure polycrystalline samples.

label: Biaxially textured metal substrates for YBCO tapes (1996)
summary: Goyal et al. reported a route using industrially scalable thermomechanical texturing of flexible metal substrates followed by epitaxial buffer layers and YBa2Cu3Ox films; the deposited films carried critical currents at 77 K in zero field and had field dependencies similar to epitaxial films on single-crystal ceramic substrates.

label: YBCO tricrystal half-flux evidence (1994)
summary: Tsuei et al. used scanning SQUID microscopy at 4.2 K to observe spontaneous half-flux-quantum magnetization in a YBa2Cu3O7-delta ring with three grain-boundary Josephson junctions, but not in the two-junction rings; the authors reported consistency with d-wave pairing symmetry.

label: BaZrO3 additions enhance YBCO in-field current (2004)
summary: MacManus-Driscoll et al. reported that BaZrO3 additions to pulsed-laser-deposited YBCO films improved thickness-accounted in-field critical current densities by about 1.5–2 times over roughly 1–5 T and about 5 times at 7 T in the studied single-crystal and IBAD-MgO substrate samples; the transport study used 75.5 K and associated the enhancement with stronger vortex pinning.

label: Industrial YBCO/Y2O3 tape for high-field fusion magnets
summary: Molodyk et al. reported over 300 km of 4 mm-wide YBCO wire manufactured in nine months, with most delivered to CFS. In tested B-parallel-c samples with a 40 micrometre substrate and 5 micrometre copper stabilizer per side, engineering current density exceeded 1000 A/mm² at 20 K and 20 T and 2000 A/mm² at 4.2 K and 20 T; the formulation used Y2O3 nanoparticles without c-axis-correlated nanocolumnar defects.

label: SPARC TFMC: NINT stack-in-plate magnet
summary: Hartwig et al. described the built TFMC as a no-insulation, no-twist REBCO stack-in-plate magnet using 270 km of tape, weighing 10058 kg, with 16 single-pancake modules and two termination plates. REBCO stacks occupy spiral plate channels, with single-pass supercritical-helium coolant channels on the other side; vacuum-pressure solder impregnation provides mechanical protection and thermal/electrical connectivity.

label: SPARC TFMC: 20.1 T magnet demonstration
summary: Hartwig et al. reported TFMC reaching 20.1 T peak field on the conductor at 40.5 kA terminal current, with 815 kN/m Lorentz loading on the REBCO stacks and almost 1 GPa stress accommodated by the structural case.

label: SPARC TFMC: demountable nanohm joints
summary: Hartwig et al. reported fifteen internal demountable pancake-to-pancake TFMC joints operating with resistance in the 0.5–2.0 nanohm range at 20 K and magnetic fields up to 12 T.

label: SPARC TFMC: deliberate quench caused local damage
summary: Hartwig et al. reported localized thermal damage following an intentional open-circuit TFMC quench at 31.5 kA terminal current. The TFMC was deliberately not optimized for quench resiliency, so this experiment assessed passive self-protection rather than demonstrating damage-free protection for fusion-scale NINT coils.

label: High-field REBCO fusion pathway: proposal and qualification
summary: Hartwig et al. describe a proposed fusion pathway using REBCO superconducting toroidal-field coils above 20 T peak field on the coil, corresponding to 8–12 T in the plasma center. The model-coil program qualifies representative-scale magnet technology for this pathway; stand-alone magnet qualification is distinct from demonstrated fusion electricity generation.
